summary: local-plugin offline-queue replay duplicates external webhook posts on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports duplicate POSTs to their external webhook after using the SDK offline/local-plugin mode. Symptom: while their app is offline (edge network outage), the SDK's local plugin accepts and executes tool calls locally. When network connectivity is restored, the SDK replays the queued tool calls to the Redwood control plane which in turn re-dispatches the webhook, causing duplicated external side effects (e.g., doubled order notifications).

Impact:
- Duplicate external side effects reported by customer (financial/notification duplication).
- Reproducible for long-running sessions that used local-plugin offline execution.

Expected behavior:
- If the SDK or local plugin executes a tool that has irreversible side effects, the execution should be marked/confirmed so the control plane does not re-run the tool post-reconnect. The idempotency/confirmation handshake should prevent duplicates regardless of offline execution path.

Actual behavior:
- Local plugin execution does not consistently persist the confirmation token/metadata into the SDK queue item. On reconnect, the control plane sees no confirmation and re-executes the tool, leading to duplicates.

Notes: customer is using Go SDK v1.8.2 with the optional local-plugin extension. They also have a TypeScript microservice that receives the webhook posts. The customer indicated the local plugin was developed in-house to forward tool calls to an on-prem subsystem when the device was offline.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure Go SDK v1.8.2 with local-plugin enabled. local-plugin accepts tool invocations and returns success without calling Redwood confirm endpoint.
2) Simulate offline network (block outbound to api.redwood.ai) and invoke a tool that triggers an external webhook (e.g., POST /orders).
3) Confirm local-plugin returns success and the SDK enqueues the tool call as 'locally-executed' in the offline queue.
4) Restore network connectivity. Observe SDK reconnect flow and replay of queued entries to the control plane.
5) Verify duplicate POSTs on customer webhook receiver and two separate tool-execution records in the control plane / logs (one local, one replayed).
logs: 2026-03-09T18:30:05Z [go-sdk] network restored, attempting reconnect to api.redwood.ai
investigation_notes: - Reproduced locally using provided repro harness and customer's local-plugin mock. Behavior matches customer reports.

- Root cause hypothesis: offline execution path does not attach/serialize the confirmation token or idempotency metadata into the SDK's persisted offline queue item. On reconnect the control plane treats the replay as a fresh invocation.

- Observed inconsistent presence of idempotency header in replayed requests; local executions sometimes include no idempotency key header because the local-plugin response path didn't propagate it back to the SDK persistence layer.

- Edge case: when the local-plugin returns a confirmation URL or token, the SDK still failed to persist that token for items created prior to v1.9.0 (regression introduced in v1.8.0 local-queue refactor).

- Querying webhook logs shows two distinct deliveries with different Redwood dispatch IDs; neither is suppressed by control-plane idempotency checks because the second request lacks the confirmation metadata expected by the dispatcher.
comments: 2026-03-10 - David (BrightCart): We saw 30 duplicate order notifications during yesterday's edge outage; this impacted billing reconciliation. We can share logs and the local-plugin code. Need urgent mitigation.
2026-03-10 - Sofia (Support): Thanks David — please attach the SDK logs (client side) and local-plugin trace. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you're using the built-in confirm endpoint?
2026-03-11 - David (BrightCart): Confirm Go SDK v1.8.2. Our local-plugin simply returns success; it was never wired to call a confirm endpoint. We assumed the SDK would mark the item as executed.

2026-03-11 - Lucas (SRE): Reproduced with customer's mock. Filing internal follow-up INT-92214 to track product fix (persist confirmation token in offline queue and attach idempotency metadata to replay).
2026-03-12 - Maya Chen (Eng): Preliminary patch ready to persist confirmation_token into offline queue item on local execution. Will open PR and run regression tests across SDK languages.
resolution:
Workaround: Instructed customer to do one of the following until patch is released:
- Disable local-plugin offline execution for tool calls that produce irreversible side effects (set allowLocalExecution=false for those actions).
- Modify local-plugin to call Redwood's confirm endpoint immediately after local execution (confirm URL + token) so control plane sees execution and suppresses replay.

Short-term fix implemented: Engineering produced a patch (PR linked above) that ensures confirmation_token is persisted alongside the offline queue item and that replay attaches idempotency/confirmation metadata for dispatch. Patch targeted for SDK rollouts: Go v1.9.0, TS v2.4.1.

Follow-ups: INT-92214 tracks audits and a test matrix to cover offline-plugin handshake, plus docs update in SDK offline-mode guide to call out explicit confirm behavior and recommended patterns for irreversible side effects.
customer_impact_summary: BrightCart experienced duplicate external notifications during an outage window. Issue affects local-plugin offline execution without confirm calls and can lead to duplicated irreversible side effects.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to merge PR and schedule SDK patch releases (Go v1.9.0, TS v2.4.1).
2) CS to coordinate a migration window with BrightCart for SDK upgrade and to validate no further duplicates in a canary session.
3) Docs update to offline-mode best practices and explicit examples for confirm endpoint use.
4) Postmortem/lessons learned to be linked to the incident report if duplicates led to material customer loss.
